subject: [APAC edge] Planned rolling node swap & driver compatibility window — action and canary ask
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Sam Li <sam.li@cloudcorp.com>, ops@cloudcorp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 03:15:00 +08:00
Subject: [APAC edge] Planned rolling node swap & driver compatibility window — action and canary ask

Hi Sam / CloudCorp ops team,

Following our walkthrough last week, we have scheduled a controlled maintenance window for APAC edge locations to apply driver shim updates (v2.14.0 -> v2.16.1) and perform a rolling host swap for a small set of older nodes that have shown elevated IO error counters under prolonged spike workloads. This is a planned, rolling change designed to avoid region-wide outages.

Summary
- Scope: 12 hosts in apac-edge-1 pool serving CloudCorp production routes + control-plane agents.
- Window: 2027-04-03 00:30–04:30 (UTC+8) — we expect each host to be drained, updated, and returned in 12–20 minute increments.
- Expected impact: transient request-level latency bumps (up to ~500ms) during KV-cache reconnects for a small subset of requests. We anticipate <1% of requests seeing a short-lived model restart; no customer-visible data plane changes or rekeying.

What we will do
1) Canary (2 hosts) run first 30 minutes with detailed telemetry.
2) Rolling drain → apply driver shim 2.16.1 → kernel module compatibility check → warm KV cache backfill → return host to pool.
3) Continuous health checks: per-route 5xx rate, tail latency (p99.9), and model-token throughput.

Attachments: rwd-apac-rolling-runbook-v1.2.pdf (runbook), canary-checklist-apac.csv (probe matrix).

Asks for CloudCorp ops
- Please confirm you are available for the canary window (first 30m) so we can run customer-facing smoke tests.
- If you need an opt-out for specific tenant(s) we must get that before 2027-04-01 18:00 UTC+8.

Internal ops notes
- Jordan: please validate rollback criteria below before canary.
- Marissa: CS to send a short customer advisory (1-paragraph) once schedule is confirmed.

Short rollback triggers (preliminary)
- >0.5% sustained 5xx for 5 minutes on CloudCorp routes OR
- p99.9 latency >2s sustained for 3 minutes OR
- Any unrecoverable KV-cache corruption during warmback.

Thanks — we’ll aim for a low-impact, observable rollout. Reply with ack and any additional requests.

—
Soojin Lee
Infrastructure Reliability, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 09:12:00 +08:00
Subject: Re: [APAC edge] Planned rolling node swap & driver compatibility window — action and canary ask

Hi all — quick follow-up with more concrete ops details and explicit rollback windows.

Answering Sam: the shim includes the io-path reorder stabilization (it is the primary reason for this targeted rollout). We validated it in our staging harness with the same concurrency profile as CloudCorp’s spike tests.

Concrete rollback and timing
- If a canary host fails post-update we will immediately mark it draining and shift traffic to warm spare nodes (estimated capacity restore: 4–8 minutes per host for routing + KV reconnect).
- Full rollback (re-flash to previous driver) is estimated ~18–28 minutes including rejoin and KV warmback; we use this only if warmback fails the health gates.

Canary criteria (pass -> continue)
- No increase in 5xx by >0.25% absolute and p99.9 < 1.2s for 20 continuous minutes.
- Successful KV warmback within 90s for both canary hosts.

I’ve attached the canary checklist and the runbook — follow the probes in the first 30 minutes exactly. Marissa — CS can send the customer advisory that includes the opt-out deadline. Vivek — please prepare the emergency rollback playbook snippet to paste into the runbook (we’ll keep it front and center).

—
Jordan Blake
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ack — customer advisory drafted and scheduled for 2027-03-31 18:00 UTC+8 (copy below). Sam — I included an opt-out link; please send any tenant prefixes to ops@redwood.com before the deadline.

Draft advisory (short)
Redwood will perform a rolling maintenance for APAC edge on 2027-04-03 00:30–04:30 (UTC+8). Expected customer impact is minimal; a very small fraction of requests may see brief latency increases while hosts warm caches. If you need to opt out specific tenant prefixes, reply to ops@redwood.com by 2027-04-01 18:00 (UTC+8).

Also, adding two small asks from Ops: 1) run the canary probe matrix in canary-checklist-apac.csv, 2) enable a 2-minute warmup probe immediately after host returns to pool so KV caches are prioritized for recent prefixes.

—
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
